question: Besides sharing information, what is a key goal of talking with your patients?

options.A: To replace the need for written medical records
options.B: To ensure the nurse finishes duties quickly
options.C: To build trust and reduce patient anxiety
options.D: To prevent patients from asking too many questions

explanation: Communication is so much more than just gathering data! It helps you build a warm, supportive bond that calms frightened or worried mummies. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is good communication especially vital in Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will pay their hospital bills promptly
options.B: It eliminates the need for any diagnostic laboratory tests
options.C: It bridges gaps caused by cultural, linguistic, and economic vulnerabilities
options.D: It is required only during the accreditation of the hospital

explanation: Our patients come from diverse backgrounds. Using clear, kind communication helps you bridge language and cultural gaps so everyone feels safe and understood. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is a great example of non-verbal communication?

options.C: Giving health talks in the antenatal clinic
options.D: Writing admission notes in the case folder

explanation: Spot on! Non-verbal communication is all about your physical gestures, facial expressions, and posture—how you carry yourself without speaking words. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h2)

question: A laboring woman is talking to you, but you keep checking your watch and tapping your foot. How will she most likely feel?

options.A: The patient will feel rushed and unsafe
options.B: The patient will relax because she sees urgency
options.C: The patient will understand the midwife is busy
options.D: The patient will start speaking much faster

explanation: Actions really do speak louder than words. When our body language shows impatience, mothers pick up on it quickly and may feel neglected or anxious. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h2)

question: How is therapeutic communication different from a casual chat with a friend?

options.A: It only involves written notes rather than spoken dialogue
options.B: It is goal-directed and focuses entirely on the patient's well-being
options.C: It requires the nurse to share personal life stories equally
options.D: It avoids discussing medical topics completely

explanation: You've got this! Unlike everyday chit-chat, therapeutic communication is a professional tool deliberately used to support and heal your patient. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why do midwives love using open-ended questions instead of closed ones?

options.A: They guarantee a simple yes or no answer for the chart
options.B: They encourage the patient to express feelings and share their full story
options.C: They make it easier to write quick nursing notes
options.D: They prevent the patient from speaking for too long

explanation: Open-ended questions (like 'How are you feeling today?') invite mothers to share their stories in their own words, giving you wonderful clinical insights. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h3)

question: What active listening skill means repeating the patient's main point back to them in your own words?
explanation: Brilliant! Restating lets you echo the patient's core message back to them to double-check that you understood them correctly. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why is it sometimes helpful to sit in gentle silence during a difficult patient talk?

options.A: It gives the patient time to reflect and gather their thoughts
options.B: It forces the patient to give a quick yes or no answer
options.C: It shows the nurse is angry with what the patient said
options.D: It saves time during a busy hospital shift

explanation: Silence can be golden. It gives the mother the emotional breathing room she needs to process tough news without feeling rushed. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic example of an environmental barrier to communication?

options.A: Severe pain experienced by a woman in second-stage labor
options.B: Anxiety and fear about undergoing an episiotomy
options.C: Loud noises and lack of privacy in a crowded ward
options.D: Hearing loss in an elderly antenatal patient

explanation: Environmental barriers come from the physical surroundings—like a noisy, crowded ward that makes private talks difficult. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why should midwives avoid using young children as interpreters for patients who speak another language?

options.A: Hospital policies forbid children from entering the hospital premises
options.B: Children always refuse to translate clinical terms accurately
options.C: Children are usually faster than trained professional translators
options.D: It breaches confidentiality and can distort sensitive medical information

explanation: Using kids to translate puts too much weight on them, breaks patient confidentiality, and risks dangerous medical misunderstandings. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h5)

question: What does cultural competence mainly ask of a midwife?

options.A: Ignore all cultural differences to treat everyone identically
options.B: Respect and adapt to diverse patient beliefs without personal bias
options.C: Force every patient to adopt Western health practices immediately
options.D: Abandon standard nursing procedures for traditional methods

explanation: Cultural competence means keeping an open mind, showing self-awareness, and honoring the diverse beliefs of the women in your care. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h6)

question: A postpartum mum wants to use a local herbal drink alongside her hospital meds. What is your best first response as her midwife?

options.A: Explore her reasons calmly and discuss any safety risks respectfully
options.B: Confiscate the herbal mixture without offering any explanation
options.C: Scold her immediately for bringing dangerous items to the ward
options.D: Allow her to drink it freely without checking its ingredients

explanation: Wonderful approach! Calm, respectful dialogue builds trust and keeps her safe without making her feel judged or dismissed. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h6)

question: In the famous SBAR communication tool, what does the letter 'B' stand for?
explanation: You've got it! 'B' is for Background, which gives your team the quick clinical history needed for the current situation. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why is writing your care notes immediately (contemporaneous documentation) so important in midwifery?

options.A: It guarantees that the hospital will receive payment immediately
options.B: It ensures an accurate, timely record of care for patient safety and legal protection
options.C: It gives the midwife something to do during quiet night shifts
options.D: It replaces the need to give verbal handovers between shifts

explanation: Writing things down as they happen prevents memory slips and gives you a reliable, legally sound record of the care provided. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h7)
